title: Watchdog evaluations and safe-apply latches for batching & KV-cache recommendations
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: The Cost Recommender can propose batching and KV-cache configuration changes that reduce per-token cost but occasionally produce subtle quality regressions (semantic drift, decreased task accuracy, or formatting breaks) that are not visible to simple token-delta metrics. Goal: build a compact, automated 'watchdog' evaluation harness and a safe-apply latch mechanism that gates automated config changes behind measurable quality guarantees and orchestrated rollback when regressions are detected. Scope: (1) a reproducible eval suite (golden prompt corpus + task-specific checks) that runs on candidate config diffs; (2) statistical acceptance thresholds and paired comparison tests; (3) a staged apply flow (shadow -> canary -> staged) with latches that abort and rollback when key metrics cross thresholds; (4) telemetry + alerting + runbook for operators. Out of scope: large-scale offline retraining or model-level tuning (handled by modelOps).
implementation_steps: Define a compact golden prompt corpus (initial 400 prompts) across common Redwood workloads: chat completions, summarization, instruction-following, and retrieval-augmented prompts; label expected outputs or evaluation predicates where applicable

Implement a lightweight evaluation runner that: 1) launches candidate configs in shadow mode; 2) collects deterministic seeds and 3) computes metrics: embedding cosine similarity (anchor), task-specific accuracy where ground truth exists, response-length and token-delta, and semantic likelihood delta (perplexity proxy)

Select statistical tests and thresholds: paired bootstrap on mean embedding similarity (alpha=0.01), require mean cosine >= 0.86 and no more than 1% absolute drop in task accuracy; disallow increases in toxic content above 0.1% false positive rate

Integrate with Cost Recommender: annotate each proposed config with evaluation result summary and a pass/fail verdict; if pass, produce a staged apply plan (shadow -> 1% canary -> 10% staged -> 100%), else mark for human review

Implement Safe-Apply Latch in orchestration: at each stage monitor live drift windows (5m and 1h) and automatically revert to previous config when metric slides beyond thresholds or a p-value indicates regression
Add observability: per-route token-level breakdown, diff examples, daily report in Console; expose a single-click ‘re-run golden suite’ action for SEs
Author runbook pages (Confluence) and Kibana dashboards; create alerting rules and Slack playbook for PagerDuty escalation
success_criteria: Golden-corpus runner can execute end-to-end within 12 minutes for a candidate config
Automated gated applies run without manual intervention for >= 70% of low-risk configs in first two weeks
No SE-logged customer regressions attributable to automated applies in first 30 days at canary scale
Rollback automation reduces median remediation time from 48 minutes to < 6 minutes for flagged regresses
risks_and_mitigation: False negatives in small golden set: mitigate by expanding corpus incrementally using active failure mining and traffic-sampled prompts
Overly strict thresholds causing constant human reviews: expose tunable policy with tiered sensitivity for prod vs sandbox tenants
Metric gaming (recommender overfitting to corpus): randomize example seeds and include adversarial prompts from customer telemetry
Performance cost of shadowing: cap shadow traffic to 5% and prioritize low-latency paths for production-sensitive models
